source_material: Published randomized 2x2 factorial design, bias-control, outcome and statistical-analysis sections
Published participant flow, baseline table and supplementary-material link

study_assessment.notes: Custom study-level appraisal complementing result-specific RoB 2. Computer-generated randomized allocation, concealed sequence and blinded outcome assessment are reported. Published analyses appear to use the 138 completers from 162 randomized participants without a reported ITT or missing-outcome sensitivity analysis. No prospective trial-registration identifier or preserved statistical-analysis plan is reported in the article. The combined arm also received greater total intervention exposure than either single-intervention arm; this limits interpretation of combination superiority but is not itself converted into a RoB 2 domain penalty. This is not a validated external quality score.

domains.domain_label: Design and randomization documentation
domains.supporting_text: Participants were randomized by computer-generated random numbers to four factorial cells; the randomization sequence was concealed from research staff and baseline characteristics were comparable across groups.

domains.domain_label: Masking and assessment separation
domains.supporting_text: Outcome assessments were conducted by trained assessors blinded to group allocation, and intervention delivery and outcome assessment were performed by different research staff.

domains.domain_label: Participant flow and post-randomization loss
domains.supporting_text: 162 participants were randomized and 138 completed the 12-week study (14.8% attrition). Attrition differed numerically across groups and the article reports voluntary withdrawal, loss to follow-up and health-related reasons, but no ITT or missing-outcome sensitivity analysis is reported.

domains.domain_label: Outcome measurement documentation
domains.supporting_text: A standardized cognitive battery was administered at baseline and post-intervention in a fixed sequence by blinded assessors using established instruments for global cognition, memory, attention, executive function, language and visuospatial performance.

domains.domain_label: Analysis, registration and transparency
domains.supporting_text: The article specifies change-score factorial ANOVA, interaction tests and Sidak-corrected simple effects, but no prospective trial-registration identifier or preserved statistical-analysis plan is reported despite multiple cognitive outcomes and eligible analytic choices.

result_assessments.estimand_or_result_scope: Effects of randomized factorial assignment to Baduanjin and/or cognitive training on post-intervention change in global cognition.
result_assessments.notes: Outcome-scoped RoB 2 appraisal for the randomized factorial global-cognition result. Stage 5 contains the four factorial cells but no privileged contrast; this appraisal does not create or alter a contrast. D3 is some concerns because 24 of 162 randomized participants were absent from the reported completer analyses without a reported ITT or missing-outcome sensitivity analysis. D5 is some concerns because no prospective registry/SAP is reported for the multiple eligible cognitive outcomes and analyses.

domains.domain_label: Bias arising from the randomization process
domains.supporting_text: Computer-generated random numbers, concealment of the randomization sequence from research staff and comparable baseline characteristics support a low-risk randomization judgement.

domains.domain_label: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domains.supporting_text: Interventions were delivered by trained staff using standardized protocols and manuals; no systematic trial-context crossover or other assignment-related deviation affecting the effect-of-assignment estimand was reported.

domains.domain_label: Bias due to missing outcome data
domains.supporting_text: 162 participants were randomized and 138 completed post-intervention assessment. Attrition was 14.8% overall, with group-specific completion of 35/43, 36/40, 34/41 and 33/38; no ITT or sensitivity analysis for missing outcomes was reported.

domains.domain_label: Bias in measurement of the outcome
domains.supporting_text: Global cognition was measured with the standardized MoCA by trained assessors blinded to randomized group, with the same procedures across assessment sessions.

domains.domain_label: Bias in selection of the reported result
domains.supporting_text: The article specifies the reported change-score factorial ANOVA and simple-effects procedure, but no prospective registry/SAP is reported despite multiple cognitive outcomes, interaction tests and eligible analytic specifications.

result_assessments.estimand_or_result_scope: Effects of randomized factorial assignment to Baduanjin and/or cognitive training on post-intervention change in long-delay memory.
result_assessments.notes: Outcome-scoped RoB 2 appraisal for long-delay memory. The result shares the trial-level randomization, deviation and attrition structure of the global-cognition result. D5 remains some concerns because the article reports many cognitive subdomains and no prospective registry/SAP is reported to establish the prespecified analytic path for this specific result.

domains.domain_label: Bias arising from the randomization process
domains.supporting_text: Computer-generated random numbers, concealed sequence and comparable baseline characteristics support a low-risk randomization judgement.

domains.domain_label: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domains.supporting_text: Standardized supervised intervention delivery was reported and no systematic trial-context deviation from randomized assignment affecting this effect-of-assignment result was identified.

domains.domain_label: Bias due to missing outcome data
domains.supporting_text: The published post-intervention analyses are based on 138 completers from 162 randomized participants, with no reported ITT or missing-outcome sensitivity analysis.

domains.domain_label: Bias in measurement of the outcome
domains.supporting_text: Long-delay memory was assessed within the standardized AVLT-H battery by trained assessors blinded to randomized group using the same post-intervention procedure across groups.

domains.domain_label: Bias in selection of the reported result
domains.supporting_text: Long-delay memory is explicitly reported within the cognitive battery, but no prospective registry/SAP is reported to rule out selection among multiple memory subdomains, factorial effects and simple-effect analyses.

result_assessments.estimand_or_result_scope: Effects of randomized factorial assignment to Baduanjin and/or cognitive training on the post-intervention executive-function, language and visuospatial results represented by this normalized outcome bundle.
result_assessments.notes: The normalized Registry outcome bundles several author-reported cognitive domains that share the same randomized factorial design and appraisal pattern. This assessment does not imply that the measures are one composite estimand; it records the common RoB pattern for the currently normalized bundle. D3 and D5 remain some concerns for the same reasons as the other post-intervention results.

domains.domain_label: Bias arising from the randomization process
domains.supporting_text: Computer-generated randomized allocation, concealed sequence and comparable baseline characteristics support low risk for the common randomization process.

domains.domain_label: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domains.supporting_text: Standardized supervised delivery and no reported systematic assignment-related deviations support low risk for the effect-of-assignment interpretation.

domains.domain_label: Bias due to missing outcome data
domains.supporting_text: The executive, language and visuospatial post-intervention analyses are reported for the 138 completers from 162 randomized participants without a reported ITT or missing-outcome sensitivity analysis.

domains.domain_label: Bias in measurement of the outcome
domains.supporting_text: TMT-B, BNT and CDT were administered as standardized cognitive measures by trained outcome assessors blinded to randomized group.

domains.domain_label: Bias in selection of the reported result
domains.supporting_text: The article reports these cognitive domains and its factorial/simple-effects approach, but no prospective registry/SAP is reported to rule out selective choice among multiple domain outcomes and analytic specifications.
